steps.q: Does it make a great product or service?

views.text: In February 2025, Equity Mates noted AMP runs a shareholder discount program offering home loan discounts and fee waivers, but also said mortgage brokers rarely found AMP among the most competitive offers, pointing to mixed appeal of its retail banking products.

episode.title: Bad news for banks & miners, where did all the dividends go & stocks with freebies

views.text: In November 2022, a guest on Equity Mates outlined AMP's product mix as AMP Bank, New Zealand Wealth Management, AMP Super and an advice platform, plus minority stakes in two Chinese businesses and a US property platform, showing a broad but complex service offering.

steps.q: Will it keep earning above market profits?

views.text: In October 2024, Equity Mates highlighted AMP’s near $7 billion in net outflows over 12 months despite the superannuation tailwind, indicating customers and advisers were shifting away and raising questions about AMP’s competitive position.

episode.title: Ren's portfolio revamp: VAS is gone! & Pimp my Portfolio with Adam Dawes

views.text: In November 2022, Equity Mates recapped that AMP’s advice model was hit by the Royal Commission, with advisers leaving and the business model challenged, framing concerns about the company’s ability to sustain advantages in advice and wealth.

In July 2021, a guest on Equity Mates said the industry shift allowed newer platforms like Hub24 and Netwealth to gobble up business as AMP declined, illustrating how quickly incumbents could lose share when technology and models changed.

steps.q: Can it reinvest its profits productively?

views.text: In July 2021, a guest on Equity Mates discussed AMP as a sum-of-the-parts story and suggested AMP Bank could be sold at some stage, signalling potential portfolio reshaping and capital allocation decisions ahead.

steps.q: Can it be bought at a reasonable price?

views.text: In November 2022, a guest on Equity Mates argued AMP’s market value of about $4 billion understated the parts, estimating roughly $7 billion if valuing AMP Bank, NZ Wealth Management, AMP Super, its advice platform and offshore stakes separately.

In July 2021, a guest on Equity Mates noted a prior non-binding approach at $1.85 and said bank price to book and PEs had compressed, providing context for how the market might value AMP and any asset sales.
